facts.label: Aula para iniciantes
facts.sub: Nos EUA há aulas de salsa para adultos em muitas cidades. As turmas de iniciantes costumam ser para quem nunca dançou. O professor mostra o básico e conta os passos em voz alta, então pergunte sem medo.

facts.label: Roupa e sapato
facts.sub: Para a primeira aula, roupas confortáveis e sapatos que deslizem um pouco costumam bastar. Você não precisa comprar sapatos de dança logo. Se tiver dúvida, pergunte ao estúdio antes: “What should I wear?”

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In many beginner dance classes, you do not have to bring a partner.
items.why: Many classes change partners during the lesson.

items.s: You have to be a good dancer before your first class.
items.why: Beginner classes are for people who have never danced.

items.s: Salsa music often has a strong beat that you count in eights.
items.why: Teachers count “one, two, three, five, six, seven” in many classes.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: In many beginner dance classes, you do not have to bring a partner. → Verdadeiro (Many classes change partners during the lesson.)
You have to be a good dancer before your first class. → Falso (Beginner classes are for people who have never danced.)
Salsa music often has a strong beat that you count in eights. → Verdadeiro (Teachers count “one, two, three, five, six, seven” in many classes.)

pages.title: Salsa on Friday · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday night, and Ana is at a salsa class. The room is big, and the music is loud. The teacher is Cole. Ana has never danced salsa before. Many people are there, and everyone looks happy.
“Welcome to salsa class!” Cole says. “**Do I have to bring a partner?**” Ana asks. “No, you don’t have to,” Cole says. “Find a partner here, and stand in line.”

pages.title: Salsa on Friday · 2/3
paragraphs: Cole asks, “**May I dance with you?**” “Sure! I’m Ana,” she says. “We start with the basics,” Cole says. “You have to listen to the music. You don’t have to be perfect.”
Ana moves her feet and counts. “One, two, three. Five, six, seven.” Her partner turns, and she steps on his foot. “Sorry!” she says. “**Slow down, please**,” Cole says. “Do you have to move so fast?”

items.why: Questions with have to use do/does.

opts: You have to listen to the music.

items.why: Listen needs to: listen to. And don’t have to means not necessary.
